spec: P4-E cost/latency optimization — measurement spec (no optimization executed here)
status: FROZEN — metrics, method, baselines, and decision rule pinned before any optimization work. No change after work starts.
question: Can we achieve useful verification performance economically without training? (And if not, exactly when does training become economically justified?)

method.latency_tokens: Read from run artifacts (latency_s, tokens, elapsed_s). Wall-clock on the same local CPU host unless stated.
method.cpu_ram: Not logged per task in P3 artifacts: instrument from the next run (method: process peak RSS + wall time per case/sample). Baseline TBD.
method.verifier_runtime: Not separately logged in P3 artifacts (verdicts carry no timings): instrument from the next run (method: time each verify() call). Baseline TBD.
method.closure_iterations: Recorded rounds (plain recipe) or 1.0 for single-pass pipeline runs.
method.candidate_count: k=5 (frozen pipeline) or BoN width for plain runs.
method.cost_cash: Measured spend ($0 to date). Rented-GPU equivalents use R-5 reference rates only.
method.success: Frozen bars only (closes/accuracy + 0 false acceptances). Never redefined.

baselines.source: Frozen P3 evidence (recomputed 2026-10-11; means over completed samples/cases)

decision_rule.optimization_accepted_iff: Cost or latency improves vs the matching baseline AND success rate does not regress AND false acceptances stay 0, all measured on frozen benchmarks.
decision_rule.training_link: If optimization plateaus above the R-5 break-even gates with a measured capability shortfall remaining, that shortfall — quantified here — becomes the training-justification evidence for a future P4-TRAIN proposal. P4-E itself never proposes training.

guardrails: No benchmark, bar, or verifier changes to improve numbers (that is grading one's own homework).
No training, no training spend, no training authorization (P4-SYS rules).
Every optimization claim ships with before/after measurements on the same frozen cases.
